title: Software-clearable lock bit
provenance: Locally authored configuration-lock register with an injected defect (lock bit writable to 0), modelled on CWE-1231. Written for SiliconBreak X; not a historical bug in any product.
license: Same license as this repository (authored here)
description: An 8-bit configuration register protected by a software-set LOCK bit in a CONTROL register. Once locked, configuration must stay frozen until reset.

security_contract.summary: Once software sets LOCK, neither the lock nor the configuration can be changed until reset.

properties.text: After LOCK is set, locked stays 1 until reset; no register write can clear it.
While locked, writes to CONFIG do not change config_out.

functional_contract.text: Reset clears config_out to 0x00 and locked to 0; writes during reset are ignored.
While unlocked, a CONFIG write updates config_out on the same clock edge.
Writing CONTROL with bit 0 = 1 sets the lock; reset clears it again.

tests.title: 3000 random cycles match the contract model while unlocked
Clearing LOCK does not reopen CONFIG
Lock properties hold on 3000 random cycles

ground_truth.summary: A CONTROL write assigns wr_data[0] to the lock, so writing 0 unlocks the register.
